trees_graphs.overview: Trees & Graphs are the highest-weight DSA area for Principal interviews. Master traversals first, then graph patterns (BFS/DFS, topo sort, shortest path).

cards.title: Graph BFS vs DFS — When to Use
cards.body:
**BFS** → shortest path in unweighted graphs, level-order, spreading infection.

**DFS** → path existence, cycle detection, connected components, backtracking on graphs.

**Memory anchor:** BFS uses a **queue** (layer by layer). DFS uses a **stack/recursion** (go deep first).

cards.title: Tree Traversals (Iterative + Recursive)
cards.body:
**Inorder** (LNR): BST → sorted order.
**Preorder** (NLR): copy tree, prefix expressions.
**Postorder** (LRN): delete tree, postfix.

Iterative inorder: stack + go left, pop, go right.

Interview tip: always state time **O(n)** and space **O(h)** for recursion.

cards.title: Topological Sort & Cycle Detection
cards.body:
**Kahn's (BFS):** in-degree count → queue nodes with 0 in-degree → reduce neighbors.
**DFS:** mark visiting/visited; back-edge to visiting node = cycle.

Use for: course schedule, build order, dependency resolution.

cards.title: Shortest Path Quick Ref
cards.body:
| Algorithm | Use when |
|---|---|
| BFS | Unweighted shortest path |
| Dijkstra | Non-negative weights |
| Bellman-Ford | Negative edges OK |
| Union-Find | Connected components |

arrays_strings.overview: Arrays & Strings power 40%+ of screening rounds. Two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums, and hash maps are your core toolkit.

cards.title: Two Pointers Pattern
cards.body:
**Sorted array pair sum** → left/right pointers move inward.
**Palindrome** → skip non-alphanumeric, compare ends.
**3Sum** → fix one element, two-pointer on remainder.

Signal: sorted input or 'find pair/triplet'.

cards.title: Sliding Window
cards.body:
Maintain a window [start, end] that satisfies a condition.

**Fixed window:** max sum of size k.
**Variable window:** longest substring without repeat — shrink when duplicate seen.

Template: expand right, while invalid shrink left.

cards.title: Kadane's — Maximum Subarray
cards.body:
At each element: **start fresh or extend?**
`currentSum = max(num, currentSum + num)`

**Hiking trail analogy:** drop negative baggage, restart from here.

Time O(n), Space O(1).

cards.title: Prefix Sum + HashMap
cards.body:
Subarray sum = K → track running prefix sums.
Identity: `sum(i..j) = prefix[j] - prefix[i-1]`

Initialize map with `{0: 1}` for empty prefix.

dp.overview: DP = optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems. Start with 1D, graduate to 2D and state machines.

cards.title: 1D DP Patterns
cards.body:
**Climbing stairs / Fibonacci:** `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]`
**House robber:** `dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i])`

Optimize space to O(1) with two variables when only last 2 states matter.

cards.title: 2D DP — Grid & LCS
cards.body:
**Grid paths:** `dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]`
**LCS:** if match → diagonal+1, else max(up, left).

Draw the table in interviews — it buys thinking time.

cards.title: Knapsack Variants
cards.body:
**0/1 Knapsack:** iterate capacity backwards to avoid reuse.
**Unbounded:** iterate forwards (reuse allowed).
**Subset sum:** special case of 0/1.

heaps.overview: Heaps solve 'K largest/smallest' and streaming median problems in O(n log k).

cards.title: Top-K Elements
cards.body:
Use **min-heap of size K** for K largest (root = smallest of top K).
Use **max-heap** for K smallest.

Time: O(n log k) — better than full sort O(n log n) when k << n.

cards.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
cards.body:
Push head of each list into min-heap. Pop smallest, push its next node.

Alternative: divide-and-conquer merge pairs.

bit_manipulation.overview: Bit tricks appear less often but are fast wins when they do — XOR for pairs, masks for subsets.

cards.title: XOR Tricks
cards.body:
`a ^ a = 0`, `a ^ 0 = a` → find single number in pairs.
**Brian Kernighan:** `n & (n-1)` clears lowest set bit — count bits.

Bitmask DP: iterate subsets of mask.

design_patterns.overview: Patterns emerge from requirements — never force them. Name the pattern out loud in LLD interviews.

cards.title: Strategy Pattern
cards.body:
Behavior varies by type → encapsulate algorithms behind interface.
**Gym example:** SilverPlan, GoldPlan each implement `getMonthlyFee()`.

Trigger: 'different pricing/perks per tier'.

cards.title: Factory Pattern
cards.body:
Centralize object creation based on input type.
`MembershipPlanFactory.create(Tier.GOLD)` — adding new tier = one new class.

cards.title: Observer Pattern
cards.body:
One-to-many notification on state change.
Membership expires → notify billing, email, analytics.

cards.title: Singleton Pitfalls
cards.body:
Thread-safe options: enum singleton, static holder, or synchronized lazy init.
**Avoid** in tests — prefer DI instead.

Karat tip: mention when you'd use DI over Singleton.

oop_solid.overview: SOLID + composition over inheritance is the backbone of every LLD round.

cards.title: LLD Interview Framework (9 Steps)
cards.body:
1. **CLARIFY** — never assume scope
2. **IDENTIFY NOUNS** → classes
3. **IDENTIFY VERBS** → methods
4. **RELATIONSHIPS** — is-a vs has-a
5. **PATTERNS** — emerge from requirements
6. **SKELETON** — interfaces first
7. **CODE** — narrate while typing
8. **TEST** — happy + edge cases
9. **EXTEND** — 'if X changed, I'd touch Y'

cards.title: SOLID One-Liners
cards.body:
**S** — one class, one reason to change
**O** — extend via new classes, don't edit old ones
**L** — subclasses honor parent contract
**I** — small focused interfaces
**D** — depend on abstractions (Spring DI!)

cards.title: Composition Over Inheritance
cards.body:
**Wrong:** `GoldMember extends Member` — can't change tier at runtime.
**Right:** `Member has-a Membership has-a Plan` — upgrade = swap plan.

Rule: inheritance only when relationship is fixed for object's lifetime.

classic_lld.overview: Classic LLD problems repeat across companies. Learn the entity model + patterns for each.

cards.title: Parking Lot — Entity Model
cards.body:
**Entities:** ParkingLot, Floor, Spot (type: compact/large/handicapped), Vehicle, Ticket.
**Patterns:** Factory for spot assignment, Strategy for pricing by vehicle type.
**Key:** Spot is-a or has-a type; Vehicle parks in compatible spot.

cards.title: Elevator System
cards.body:
**Entities:** Building, Elevator, Request (floor, direction), Controller.
**Patterns:** State (idle/moving/door open), Strategy (SCAN vs FCFS dispatch).
**Concurrency:** queue requests, one elevator handles one direction sweep.

cards.title: LRU Cache — Karat Mini Build
Splitwise / Expense Sharing
cards.body:
**Entities:** User, Group, Expense, Split (equal/exact/percentage).
**Key:** minimize transactions via debt simplification (graph / greedy).
**Pattern:** Strategy for split types.

concurrency_lld.overview: Concurrency in LLD: thread-safe collections, producer-consumer, rate limiting.

cards.title: Rate Limiter — Token Bucket
cards.body:
Refill tokens over time; `tryAcquire()` decrements if available.
Synchronize `tryAcquire` for thread safety.

Distributed follow-up: Redis + Lua script for atomic decrement.

cards.title: Producer-Consumer
cards.body:
BlockingQueue decouples producer and consumer.
`put()` blocks when full; `take()` blocks when empty.

Alternative: wait/notify with bounded buffer.

cards.title: Concurrent Collections
cards.body:
Default to `ConcurrentHashMap` over synchronized HashMap.
`CopyOnWriteArrayList` for read-heavy, rare writes.
`ArrayDeque` preferred over Stack/LinkedList for stack/queue.

fundamentals.overview: System design fundamentals: CAP, caching, load balancing, DB scaling.

cards.title: CAP Theorem
cards.body:
Pick 2 of 3: **Consistency**, **Availability**, **Partition tolerance**.
In practice P is unavoidable → choose CP (banking) vs AP (social feeds).

Mention consistency models: strong, eventual, causal.

cards.title: Caching Layers
cards.body:
**CDN** — static assets at edge.
**Redis** — hot data, sessions, rate limits.
**Cache-aside:** app reads cache → miss → DB → populate.
**Write-through:** write cache + DB together.

cards.title: Load Balancing
cards.body:
L4 (TCP) vs L7 (HTTP) balancing.
Algorithms: round-robin, least connections, consistent hashing (for caches).

messaging.overview: Kafka and event-driven architecture are Principal-level must-knows.

cards.title: Kafka Internals
cards.body:
**Topic** → **Partitions** (parallelism) → **Offsets** (per consumer).
Consumer groups: each partition consumed by one consumer in group.
Retention: time or size based.

cards.title: Delivery Semantics
cards.body:
**At-most-once:** fire and forget.
**At-least-once:** retry + dedup (idempotency keys).
**Exactly-once:** transactional producer + idempotent consumer (hard, expensive).

classic_hld.overview: Classic HLD: URL shortener, feed, chat, video — know the data model and scaling bottlenecks.

cards.title: URL Shortener
cards.body:
**Write path:** hash → base62 encode → store mapping.
**Read path:** redirect via cache (Redis) → DB fallback.
**Scale:** read-heavy → cache + CDN; shard by hash prefix.

cards.title: News Feed / Timeline
cards.body:
**Fan-out on write** (push) vs **fan-out on read** (pull).
Hybrid: push for celebrities, pull for normal users.
**Storage:** user timeline = sorted post IDs.

cards.title: Chat System
cards.body:
**WebSocket** for real-time; **message queue** for persistence.
**Online presence:** heartbeat + Redis set.
**Ordering:** per-conversation sequence numbers.

scalability.overview: Scaling patterns: horizontal vs vertical, microservices tradeoffs, resilience.

cards.title: Horizontal vs Vertical
cards.body:
**Vertical:** bigger machine — simple but ceiling.
**Horizontal:** more machines — needs load balancing, stateless services, shared storage.

cards.title: Circuit Breaker & Bulkhead
cards.body:
**Circuit breaker:** stop calling failing service (closed → open → half-open).
**Bulkhead:** isolate thread pools so one failure doesn't cascade.

jvm.overview: JVM internals for senior Java interviews — memory model, GC, JIT.

cards.title: JVM Memory Model
cards.body:
**Heap:** objects (young gen: Eden/S0/S1, old gen).
**Stack:** frames, local vars per thread.
**Metaspace:** class metadata (post Java 8).

cards.title: GC Algorithms
cards.body:
**G1:** default, region-based, predictable pauses.
**ZGC/Shenandoah:** sub-ms pauses, large heaps.

Know: minor GC (young), major GC (old), stop-the-world.

spring.overview: Spring Boot essentials for full-stack Karat and onsite rounds.

cards.title: Dependency Injection
cards.body:
Spring IoC container manages bean lifecycle.
**Constructor injection** preferred (immutable, testable).
`@Autowired` on constructor — dependencies explicit.

cards.title: Transaction Management
cards.body:
`@Transactional` — proxy wraps method in DB transaction.
Rollback on RuntimeException by default.
Propagation: REQUIRED (default), REQUIRES_NEW, NESTED.

cards.title: Consensus (Raft Overview)
cards.body:
Leader election → log replication → commit when majority acks.
Used in: etcd, Consul. Simpler mental model than Paxos.

cards.title: Idempotency Patterns
cards.body:
Idempotency key per request → store result in Redis.
Duplicate request returns cached response.
Critical for payments and message consumers.

star_stories.overview: STAR format for behavioral rounds. Prepare 5 stories you can adapt.

cards.title: STAR Framework
cards.body:
**S**ituation — 1 sentence context
**T**ask — your specific responsibility
**A**ction — what YOU did (use 'I', not 'we')
**R**esult — quantified outcome

Keep each story to 2 minutes. Principal stories need technical depth.

cards.title: Conflict Resolution Story
cards.body:
Pick a real disagreement on technical approach.
Show: listened first, data-driven decision, outcome for team.
Avoid: blaming others or 'I was right'.

principal_topics.overview: Principal-level: architecture decisions, team scaling, technical vision.

cards.title: Architecture Decision Framework
cards.body:
1. Context & constraints
2. Options considered (at least 2)
3. Tradeoffs table
4. Decision + rationale
5. Revisit criteria

Document as ADR (Architecture Decision Record).

company_research.overview: Research target company before interviews — shows genuine interest.

cards.title: Questions to Ask Interviewer
cards.body:
- What does success look like in first 90 days?
- Biggest technical challenge the team faces?
- How are architecture decisions made?
- Engineering culture around on-call and quality?

microLessons.title: Karat Communication Script
microLessons.body:
For every problem:
1. **Restate** in your own words
2. **Clarify** edge cases
3. **State brute force** first
4. **State optimization** before coding
5. **Narrate** while typing
6. **State complexity** unprompted
7. **Test** with sample input

Narrated partial completion beats silent rushed completion.

microLessons.title: Extension Question Chains
microLessons.body:
Karat's signature: solve Part 1, then interviewer extends.

Examples:
- Two Sum → sorted array → 3Sum
- Rate limiter → distributed Redis
- LRU cache → implement without LinkedHashMap

Budget time: working Part 1 + attempted Part 2 > perfect Part 1 alone.

microLessons.title: DSA Pattern Triggers
microLessons.body:
| Signal | Technique |
|---|---|
| Sorted + O(log n) | Binary Search |
| Pair/triplet sum | Two Pointers / HashMap |
| Subarray condition | Sliding Window |
| Frequency count | HashMap |
| K largest | Min-Heap size K |
| All combinations | Backtracking |

microLessons.title: Stuck in LLD? Recovery Script
microLessons.body:
Never go silent >10 seconds.

Say: 'Let me think through entities first...'
Sketch nouns on paper.
Pick the simplest pattern that fits.
'If I had more time, I'd add X.'

Interviewers grade thinking process, not just code.

microLessons.title: equals() + hashCode() Contract
microLessons.body:
Equal objects MUST have same hashCode.
Override both together or HashMap lookups break silently.
Use same fields in both methods.

Karat pick-2-of-5 favorite question.

microLessons.title: Composition Over Inheritance
microLessons.body:
Member has-a Membership has-a Plan.
NOT GoldMember extends Member.

Upgrade tier = swap plan reference.
This is the #1 mistake in gym membership LLD interviews.

microLessons.title: Daily Study Habit
microLessons.body:
15 minutes daily beats 3-hour weekend cramming.
Today's Focus = forward motion.
Today's Revision = retention.
Micro-lesson = one new insight.

You're building interview muscle memory.
